  "source": "Bernstein",
  "title": "AI Data Center Interconnects: Copper Inside, Optical Outside, CPO in Between (webinar recap)",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-10-18",
  "insights": [
   "AI workloads are fundamentally altering data center interconnect architecture, shifting requirements from traditional copper-heavy designs to a mix of copper for short-reach scale-up and single-mode optics for long-reach scale-out.",
   "The industry framework is 'copper inside, optics outside, CPO in between,' with copper remaining the dominant medium for short-reach rack connectivity due to cost and technical viability.",
   "Physics limits copper reach as signaling speeds increase; passive copper reach compresses to ~18 inches at 200Gbps and ~12 inches at 400Gbps, necessitating a transition to optics for longer distances.",
   "Co-packaged optics (CPO) addresses switch-level constraints by moving electrical-to-optical conversion adjacent to the switch silicon, reducing the electrical path from ~18 inches to ~0.5 inches.",
   "CPO adoption is expected to be gradual, with meaningful practical adoption starting from 2030+ as the manufacturing ecosystem for silicon photonics matures.",
   "Alternative architectures like co-packaged copper (CPC) and near-packaged optics (NPO) are developing in parallel to solve front-panel density and reach challenges.",
   "Inference workloads do not inherently require optics inside the rack today, and copper should continue to be used where bandwidth and reach allow.",
   "The supply chain for indium-phosphide lasers is a potential bottleneck, as ~70% of supply originates from China and AI build-outs are placing significantly greater demands on manufacturing yields."

  "insights": [
   "Deutsche Bank Research Institute (Adrian Cox, Oct 12, 20-page report 'AI boom or doom') tests the 'San Francisco Consensus' on superintelligence against physical constraints. Conclusion: the science might work, but the cost is very large and increasingly debt-funded.",
   "DB estimates training 2026's top models took 10^26 to 10^27 FLOPs. An 'AGI-like model' needing three orders of magnitude more implies a 10^30 FLOP run.",
   "Running one 10^30 FLOP training run on all of today's US AI infrastructure would take nearly four years. The infrastructure would need about 6GW, roughly 50% more than the four recently activated Vogtle nuclear units, at a cost of $300bn to $500bn.",
   "Completing the run in four months on Nvidia Vera Rubin chips would need 7.8m chips and 26GW of facility power. DB puts that at $900bn today, with a rental-equivalent cost of $90bn.",
   "If hardware cost trends hold, a 2030-era cluster able to do such a run would need about $200bn of compute and power hardware, for a training run costing about $20bn.",
   "Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle are set to invest almost $800bn of capex in 2026 and over $1 trillion a year through 2030 and beyond. That adds $4 trillion to $6 trillion of AI compute by 2030, enough for a 10^30 FLOP run 'with some comfort'.",

   "Alphabet posted its first quarterly free cash outflow in nearly two decades in its latest quarter while raising full-year capex guidance to $205bn. It also reported a $514bn backlog of contracted, not-yet-recognised data centre revenue.",
   "Gartner (Oct 14) calculates $8.5 trillion of revenue is needed through 2030 versus no more than $3.6 trillion expected. ZeroHedge says this hit the market hard this week.",

   "Dario Perkins will publish a Macro Picture this week on what happens if the AI boom ends in a bust. He calls it a scenario but concedes it is effectively a forecast. This note does not address whether AI is a bubble or when it ends, only the fallout.",
   "Perkins argues AI ecosystem revenue growth is still mostly capex recycling. Hyperscaler spending flows into the ecosystem and shows up as revenue, rather than coming from businesses and end-users outside it. He says the story is unchanged from his earlier-in-the-year analysis.",

   "AI financing leverage is rising rapidly. Hyperscaler balance sheets are described as pristine and unlikely to default, though they might not renew all rolling datacenter leases.    "AI debt is not seen as a systemic issue but could still be a problem if earnings disappoint and misses cascade through the ecosystem as cancelled orders. Tech hardware and chips are cyclical and prone to bullwhip effects. Perkins also flags NVIDIA's vendor financing as a concern.",
   "Perkins says some analysts warn of 'teaser rate' effects like subprime, though he calls the comparison stretched.
